youtube.summary: NZ First MP Casey Costello discusses the party’s priorities including tackling organised crime, strengthening border security, challenging race-based policies and reforming aged care. She also addresses the need for a more robust investigation of vaccine injuries and shares her views on representing voters and holding government to account. youtube.title: SAM BAILEY
youtube.summary: Alistair Harding interviews Dr Sam Bailey about raising $250,000 in six days to pay costs and fines imposed following Medical Council disciplinary proceedings over her Covid-era publications. Sam discusses her case, the consequences of her bankruptcy proceedings and concerns about medical regulation and freedom of expression. She also calls on listeners to write to the Medical Council to end its persecution of Doctors and restore freedom of speech for the profession. Check out Sam's YouTube advising how you can help further

youtube.title: LEGAL HUB
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Katie Ashby-Koppens about the Government’s proposed regulatory framework for natural health products, questioning whether new oversight is necessary and warning that licensing fees, ingredient restrictions and compliance costs could limit consumer choice and burden businesses. With submissions due on 2 November, they encourage New Zealanders to have their say before the incoming Government considers the proposals. Act now! Make your submission on Natural Health Products

youtube.title: TECH TUESDAY
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan and Steven Sykes look at plans for a new mobile phone tower in an Auckland residential street following changes to installation rules, alongside concerns about electromagnetic radiation and residents’ rights. They examine cyberattacks on commercial fridges, outdated software vulnerabilities, AI screening out qualified job applicants over minor CV differences and a US case raising questions about phone searches, privacy and duress codes. youtube.title: NORMAN LEWIS
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Dr Norman Lewis, Senior Research Fellow at the Freedom and Sovereignty Initiative Europe, about the EU’s Democracy Shield and Digital Services Act. Norman argues that expanding restrictions on online speech, election-related monitoring and pre-bunking initiatives risk undermining democratic accountability and suppressing dissent. He warns that growing efforts to control public debate could erode free speech, but believes ordinary people’s resistance offers grounds for optimism. Discover more from Norman on Substack and X
